mechanism_context.what_it_measures: the cuTensorNet scratch allocator's appetite, not the workload's intrinsic MPS footprint
mechanism_context.documented_behavior: NVIDIA CUDA-Q tensornet backends reserve 50% of FREE device memory for scratch space by default; customizable via CUDAQ_TENSORNET_SCRATCH_SIZE_PERCENTAGE (valid 5-95%).
mechanism_context.implication: the reading is proportional to FREE card memory and INDEPENDENT of circuit size; it partly reflects the 80 GB card, not the H20/40q MPS. On a smaller card the same run would read smaller.
mechanism_context.explains_this_A100_reading: 50% of 79.25 GB free at start ~= 39.6 GB, matching the measured device-wide peak of 40.32 GB — the mechanism explains THIS reading exactly.

demonstrating_datum_4q_smoke.note: a trivial circuit reserved the same ~40 GB pool -> confirms size-independence

attempt1_precedent_context_only.interpretation: consistent with pool domination (50% of free memory would imply ~24 GB free at the time, plausible but unverifiable); composition unknown; context only
attempt1_precedent_context_only.caveat: prior attempt-1 precedent for CONTEXT only; no verdict derived from it here. The mechanism explains the A100 reading exactly but attempt-1 only conditionally.

supplementary_diagnostic.label: DIAGNOSTIC — NOT the P3 verdict
supplementary_diagnostic.purpose: decompose the device-wide reading into allocator-appetite vs true MPS footprint by measurement: cap the cuTensorNet scratch pool via the documented knob and re-measure
supplementary_diagnostic.interpretation: With the cuTensorNet scratch pool capped at the documented 5% floor (~3.96 GB of 79.25 GB free), the IDENTICAL H20/40q chi=400 sampling completes normally (not starved; contraction 1376.5s) and peaks at 4.88 GB device-wide. Decomposition: the uncapped verdict read 40.32 GB; capping drops it to 4.88 GB, so ~35.4 GB was pure allocator appetite (the free-memory-proportional pool), and the workload's own device footprint is ~4.88 GB (capped scratch 3.96 GB + CUDA context + chi=400 MPS tensors, i.e. ~0.92 GB above the scratch cap — consistent in magnitude with the pre-registered ~0.2 GB tensor estimate once ~0.3-0.7 GB CUDA context is allowed). KEY FINDING: at a ~4 GB scratch cap the run peaks at 4.88 GB, UNDER the 8 GB threshold — so the pre-registered physics (MPS is memory-frugal) holds by measurement; the uncapped P3 FAIL is an allocator-appetite artifact of the 80 GB card, not a workload that needs >8 GB. This is a measurement, NOT the P3 verdict: the frozen P3 metric remains the uncapped device-wide 40.32 GB reading -> FAIL as-measured, threshold 8.0 GB untouched.

guardrails_honored: Threshold 8.0 GB untouched; frozen config untuned (no pool cap on the verdict run); device memory reported as measured, no host-RSS substituted; existing H100 evidence file (a24fe53) untouched; verdict is exactly what THIS measurement says.
